novelty.justification: The claim proposes that “the degree to which a candidate model is susceptible to a subliminal dataset generated by a reference model is a quantitative, black-box fingerprint of shared base-model lineage,” which is a new measurement/forensic use of subliminal-learning specificity rather than merely a new model setting. Searches for “subliminal learning base model specificity lineage fingerprint,” “steering vector distillation model provenance,” “LLM provenance fingerprint fine-tuning susceptibility,” and related terms found the closest prior work in *Subliminal Learning: Language models transmit behavioral traits via hidden signals in data* and *Subliminal Learning Is Steering Vector Distillation*, which establish or explain cross-base transfer failure, while *Model Provenance Testing for Large Language Models* and *Hide and Seek: Fingerprinting Large Language Models with Evolutionary Learning* use output-similarity or prompting signals rather than induced-trait susceptibility. The step from those works to the proposed claim requires a new core relationship—treating cross-model learning dynamics as a lineage classifier—so it is more than a direct transfer or natural object substitution; it merits 7, though it remains an inversion within established subliminal-learning and provenance frameworks rather than a paradigm-level method warranting 9–10.
